prespecification: prespec_ventricular.md — split-sample design, directions and stop rule fixed before computing
selection_problem: LV_basal and RV_basal were chosen BECAUSE they topped an 11-variable screen on this cohort. Re-testing on the same rows is circular. Primary design: rank all 11 on a random half A, test only the A-selected top-2 on held-out half B, with the permutation null computed in B.

USFM.reading: Percentil_LV_basal is selected in half A (r=+0.140) and SURVIVES in held-out half B (r=+0.124, n=383, null p95=0.067, p=0.012, BH q=0.048). Percentil_IRTms also transfers (+0.107 -> +0.086, p=0.024, q=0.048). This is the first result in this project to pass a split-sample selection test.

radiomics.reading: EVERY radiomics r_A is negative or near zero (best -0.002). There was nothing to select in half A, so its top-2 (ICTms, ETms) are arbitrary and neither transfers. The radiomics cardiac block-level 0.169 does not survive being split.

H2_specificity.reading: the prespecified specificity check holds on BOTH representations: basal percentiles are much stronger than longitudinal ones from the SAME chambers. USFM basal LV +0.165 / RV +0.070 vs longitudinal LV -0.026 / RV +0.014; radiomics basal +0.129 / +0.128 vs longitudinal +0.017 / +0.068. A global confound would lift both axes equally, so this argues against one.

VERDICT: SPLIT. The USFM arm passes its prespecified stop rule -- LV_basal is selected on one half and clears its permutation null on the other, at BH q=0.048 -- and the specificity check passes on both representations. But the radiomics arm has no A-half signal to select at all, so the two encoders DISAGREE at split-sample resolution despite agreeing at 0.963 on the raw representation. That disagreement is the reason not to call this a finding yet.
what_would_settle_it: the split is seed-dependent at n~380 per half. Repeat over 20 random splits and report the distribution of r_B: a real effect should transfer in most splits, a lucky maximum in few. That is the cheapest decisive test and it has NOT been run.
caveats: one split, one seed — the single most important limitation
LV_basal has n=755 (coverage 0.807), so each half is ~380
radiomics and USFM agree at cc=0.963 on the raw representation yet disagree here, which suggests the effect lives in a small subspace one encoder retains and the other does not
IRTms transferring alongside LV_basal was not predicted by H1 and is unexplained

TWENTY_SPLIT_REPLICATION.design: repeat the whole select-on-A / test-on-B procedure over 20 random seeds; a real effect transfers in most splits
TWENTY_SPLIT_REPLICATION.READING: LV_basal is the most-selected variable on BOTH representations (USFM 15/20, radiomics 12/20) out of 11 candidates -- chance selection into a top-2 would be ~3.6/20. On USFM it then transfers: mean held-out r_B = +0.109, significant in 13 of the 15 splits where it was selected. On radiomics it transfers much more weakly: mean r_B = +0.046, significant in only 5 of 12, and the range crosses zero (-0.082 to +0.164). The single-seed result was therefore not a lucky split -- but the encoder disagreement is systematic, not seed noise.
TWENTY_SPLIT_REPLICATION.VERDICT_AFTER_REPLICATION: LV_basal is a REAL but SMALL and ENCODER-DEPENDENT association. It is consistently the strongest of 11 cardiac variables on both representations and consistently transfers out-of-sample on USFM (r~0.11, 13/15 splits). It does not reliably transfer on radiomics (r~0.05, 5/12). Combined with the specificity check passing on both -- basal >> longitudinal from the same chambers -- this is the one image<->tabular signal in this project that has survived every control applied to it. Its effect size is r~0.11, which is small, and it rests on a single encoder.
